title: Annual check-ups and medical insurance
excerpt: Separate a clinic package from insurance conditions, verify components and protect medical information when comparing annual check-ups.

seo.title: Annual check-up and insurance conditions | ING Broker
seo.description: Compare clinic check-up components with your health programme, periods, approval, payment and documents without medical screening recommendations.

content:
A check-up is a package name that needs explanation through its services, not confirmation that every test is needed or paid by insurance. For a beneficiary in Moldova, medical advice and use under an insurance programme are different questions. The word annual settles neither by itself. A commercial calendar does not create an identical clinical need for everyone.

This page compares packages and documents administratively. It proposes no investigation list, screening frequency or diagnosis and confirms no ING Broker offer for every preventive visit. Competent professionals determine medical care. Financing needs a separate check against current documents. Insurance information should not become a reason to request unnecessary services or delay necessary care.

The clinic package and insurance programme

A clinic may group several services under a commercial name while insurance uses other categories and procedures. Obtain the detailed list and check each relevant component. Do not assume the package name is recognised as one policy service. A single price can be commercially clear without explaining how each item is considered financially.

A medical membership may have its own rules and is not automatically an insurance contract. Identify the provider, document and party undertaking payment. If an offer combines membership with insurance, request separate explanations. A partner clinic's promotion is insufficient: branches, service lists and the beneficiary's actual programme can differ. Check the current proposal and enrolled person, not a general advertisement screenshot.

Who decides which services are appropriate?

An insurance article cannot decide which investigations you should undergo. A commercial list does not replace a medical discussion. Ask a competent professional about appropriateness, then clarify the financial process. Do not request tests merely to use an available limit. The administrative purpose is understanding the route, not encouraging services without indication.

Equally, commercial uncertainty should not be turned into advice to postpone needed care. Preventive may appear differently in presentations and terms. Ask how the programme defines the category, without assigning your own clinical classification. The answer should identify the applicable document and approvals rather than a vague assurance that prevention is important. General benefit language does not establish financial acceptance.

What does annual mean in the contract?

The calendar year and policy period are not necessarily the same. Ask which period the benefit uses and how previous use is recorded. A new year or new appointment does not establish a fresh entitlement automatically. For employer benefits, check enrolment and employment changes. A company programme may follow a different period from the beneficiary's personal calendar.

At renewal, ask whether limits, services or procedures change. Keeping a name does not prove all terms continue. Retain earlier and later versions, especially where an appointment or invoice falls near transition. A new website presentation should not replace the document relevant to an older expense. Keep the applicable period identifiable throughout the request.

Booking and financial approval

Clarify direct booking versus a coordinator, required records and how an answer arrives. A clinic calendar slot does not automatically mean the insurer pays every component. If recommendations or other documents are required, establish that before use when circumstances permit. Do not alter clinical wording to fit a commercial title; the necessary explanation belongs to the competent professional.

Retain the exact scope of an answer. Confirmation for one consultation must not be extended to the entire package. Obtain separate clarification for unconfirmed services and any personal cost according to the documents. A general approved status without identifying the component can confuse booking, medical decisions and payment. Services on one day do not automatically have identical financial treatment.

Direct payment or initial payment by the beneficiary

Check the mechanism and who sends confirmation to the clinic. A provider network alone does not show that nothing is payable at reception. Ask about personal costs, limits and unaccepted components. For reimbursement, request the document list before assuming a receipt is sufficient. Itemised invoices, proof of payment and clinical documents have distinct roles.

Do not gather services under your own rewritten description. Preserve provider records. For a single-price package, ask whether component detail is required to assess programme categories. Request missing information from the issuer rather than editing the invoice or report. Retain the original alongside any clarification so later reviewers can understand what was supplied and what changed.

How to compare two packages

Start with service lists and relevant medical advice, not a large advertising count of investigations. This page does not establish clinical equivalence. Administratively, compare providers, approvals, limits and payment. Ask whether prices include the same components and what remains outside. An additional consultation or explanation of results may follow separate rules requiring clarification.

A longer list does not automatically make a package more complete for the actual need. Mark confirmed, unconfirmed and outside the programme only where documented answers support those statuses. Missing information is not a benefit. Transparent comparison is more useful than a ranking built only from price and number of services, and it does not select medical care on the reader's behalf.

If an initial service leads to further recommendations

The initial package and later services require separate insurance review. First-stage confirmation does not establish financial acceptance of everything that might follow. The clinician discusses indications; the programme explains expense procedure and evidence. Do not interpret results through a remaining financial ceiling. An available amount or exhausted benefit is not a clinical criterion.

Discuss continued care with the competent professional rather than drawing a conclusion from a commercial article. Keep each stage chronologically separate to identify what was actually assessed and why additional information was requested. A request for further evidence is neither automatically a refusal nor implicit acceptance. Retain its exact wording and the document it concerns.

A component sheet for a check-up package

Copy the clinic's exact service names into a working sheet without results or personal information. Place the programme category beside each. The aim is not choosing investigations but distinguishing a commercial bundle from financially assessed components. Medical usefulness remains a separate professional discussion. Avoid renaming items in ways that imply unverified equivalence.

  • Component: the exact clinic-list description.
  • Programme category: the relevant heading and document.
  • Status: confirmed, unconfirmed or outside, based on recorded answers.
  • Billing: a separate line or part of the package price.
  • Later clarification: who explains a list or estimate change.

A company may explain this structure without receiving employee results. Date the list and update the working copy while preserving documents for earlier requests. General network, access and data questions appear in the voluntary programme assessment. This sheet specifically tracks package components without medical rankings or unsupported productivity claims.

An example of a clear request

Instead of asking simply whether insurance pays a check-up, identify the programme and actual package list. Ask which parts are considered, whether approval is necessary and which records to keep. Results are unnecessary for a general procedural explanation. If only part receives an answer, separate remaining costs and seek clarification rather than extending the response yourself.

This illustration organises a discussion, not a recommendation of the package or confirmation of personal eligibility. It can explain who receives a request and how its scope is followed without using a real medical file. Where sensitive detail later becomes justified, establish its purpose, recipient and channel before transmission. Public forms are not full medical-record repositories.

ING Broker's role

Insurance ING Broker SRL is an insurance broker, not a clinic or source of clinical recommendations. This article confirms no annual check-up product for every person. A possible offer requires programme, eligibility and current-document review. Initially describe the administrative need and existing programme without identification records or medical results. Determine necessary evidence before sending sensitive information.

The broker can explain options within its role but does not prescribe investigations or decide an insurer's payment. Catalogue presence does not establish a separately available product. Intermediation possibilities remain a distinct question; they cannot be inferred merely from an informational page title. Clinical indications and financial acceptance must remain separate in any later discussion.

When the package list changes

A clinic may change the name or components. Keep the list actually proposed for your booking and the programme's response for that version. An older approval does not demonstrate inclusion of different services. Ask for an explanation of any replacement rather than deciding clinical or financial equivalence yourself. An unchanged price does not settle a changed content question.

For an employer communication, reflect updates in information available to employees, not only in procurement files. A message can identify where rules and question channels are found. Do not announce unconfirmed advantages or promise health outcomes. An exact dated list reduces confusion between clinic sales and the employee's contract. Updating a working copy should not delete an earlier request's evidence.

A practical transition-period check

In a hypothetical example, booking used one list and the clinic later supplies a revision. Retain both and clarify which applies to the visit. Then ask which version the financial answer addresses. Do not choose the newest file automatically as proof that every service is included, and do not amend an earlier confirmation independently.

Mark excluded or still-reviewed items individually. One appointment time does not mean one payment rule. Personal budgeting needs clear confirmed costs while medical decisions need competent advice. Before submission, check dates, programme period, service names and answer sources. This lets another responsible person follow the request without access to all results and without guessing the financial decision.

Frequently asked questions about check-ups

Does annual mean everyone needs the same tests?

No. The article sets no medical frequency or list. Care is discussed professionally, separately from contractual benefits.

Is a partner clinic's package automatically included?

Do not assume it. Check components, branch and procedure. Network presence does not confirm every service.

Can the whole package be reimbursed with one invoice?

It depends on required evidence and categories. Ask about itemisation and procedure without changing the provider's invoice.

Does initial confirmation include later investigations?

Not automatically. Further services need distinct programme checking. Medical recommendation and financial acceptance remain separate roles.

Next step
